lee: Heads-up: we pulled `halite-8b-community.tgz` for onboarding. Quick license scan shows a mixed set: model weights have a "Non-Commercial Evaluation License", tokenizer claims CC0, and model card references a third-party dataset with "attribution required". Before we start quant sweeps and end-to-end latency tests I need licensing guidance: can we 1) host an internal-only inference endpoint for benching, 2) run a small partner-facing trial under NDA, and 3) produce 4-bit quant artifacts and keep them on our infra for internal use?

lee: License excerpt pasted:
```
Non-Commercial Evaluation License 2026
- Allowed: evaluation, research, internal benchmarks.
- Disallowed: commercial offering, serving to paying customers, redistribution of model weights.
- Attribution: any public material must include the specified dataset and author attributions.
```

sophie_legal: Short answer: internal-only hosting for evaluation is fine. Partner trial under NDA is risky: many "evaluation" licenses interpret any external access (even under NDA) as distribution or public use. We should ask for an explicit exception for a time-boxed, non-commercial partner trial.

sophie_legal: Regarding quant artifacts: generating quantized files is allowed for internal evaluation, but if those files could be copied out (intentionally or accidentally) to partners/customers, that's a red flag. We need controls: restrict access, audit logs, and a technical guardrail that prevents exporting `*.q4` artifacts.

kai_ml: On the ML side: our quant pipeline creates `halite-8b-q4.bin` and a small metadata file. We rely on CI to publish official artifacts; we can keep these in an internal-only bucket. If legal requires, we can run quantization on ephemeral sandbox nodes and delete artifacts after runs, using only cached KV-keys for serving.

derek_prod: Product angle: our latency beta requires external API calls from partner infra to measure end-to-end. If vendor denies external access we lose the ability to validate latency in situ. Can legal negotiate a limited remote-test clause that only allows partner endpoints to call our internal sandbox with strict logging?

sophie_legal: Yes, request a limited Remote-Partner-Test amendment: explicitly permit (a) partner access to a managed endpoint for performance testing, (b) no persistence of model weights or quant artifacts on partner systems, and (c) audit logging of requests and partner identity. Also clarify attribution text for any public benchmarks.

lee: Also note: model performs ~3% worse on our summarization eval vs baseline on raw fp16, but quant seems to amplify hallucinations. We want to run A/B evals across 4-bit configs and compare outputs. Any special consent needed for publishing those benchmark numbers internally or externally?

sophie_legal: Internally is fine. For external publication include vendor attribution and check dataset attribution clauses. If results are negative, vendor might object to public negative comparisons; check if there's a clause restricting disparagement. If present, escalate.

sec-bot: Security note: created policy exception request SEC-412 and attached requirement: encryption at rest for `halite-8b-q4.bin`, access logs retained 180 days.

lee: OK. Action items: (1) Sophie to draft amendment request (partner remote test + quant artifact retention constraints + attribution wording), (2) Kai to set quant CI to block `*.q4` uploads to external buckets and enable ephemeral-quant mode, (3) Derek to re-plan partner beta if amendment denied.

sophie_legal: Drafting now. Will ping #legal-review and loop vendor-relations + partnerships. Expect draft within 48h.

lee: thanks, hold off on wide quant runs until we get the amendment or confirm internal-only allowed. :white_check_mark:
